chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Zareeh, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you have completed your rituals, return, for it is more desirable for you to return.

key_terms.نُسُكِكَ: Your rituals (specifically referring to the rites of Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on staying in Mecca after completing Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises pilgrims to depart Mecca promptly after completing their *Nusuk* (core rituals), emphasizing that lingering unnecessarily is disliked (*makruh*). This instruction reflects the scholarly understanding that the spiritual merit of Hajj is tied to the timely completion of rites, and prolonged stay without valid reason may lead to distraction or unnecessary expenditure, aligning with the chapter's theme of 'abhorrence of staying in Makkah' beyond the required duration.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, from Zareeh, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you are free from performing your rituals, return, for it would be more desirous for you to the returning’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from those whom he has mentioned from Dharih from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When you complete your nusuk (acts of ‘Umrah and or Hajj) go back; it leaves you with more desire to return to Makkah.’”
